explained.tdh.check.metaDescription: Every day two separately written programs recompute every collector's TDH and compare it with 6529.io.
explained.tdh.check.title: The daily check
explained.tdh.check.lede: Every day the Rust core recomputes every collector's TDH from Ethereum, a separately written Python program recomputes it from the same input, and both are compared, record by record, with what 6529.io published.
explained.tdh.check.scope.rssLabel: The daily check as an RSS feed
explained.tdh.check.unread.headline: The public feed could not be read just now.
explained.tdh.check.unread.body: This page reads the daily comparison's files each time it is opened. Nothing here is shown from an older copy; try again in a few minutes.
explained.tdh.check.verdict.equal: 6529.io's TDH matches two separately written recomputations, for all {identities} identities.
explained.tdh.check.verdict.equalDetail: Every identity's TDH equals what the Rust core and the Python reference computed, to the unit, and so do all {wallets} wallets.
explained.tdh.check.verdict.knownCause: 6529.io's TDH matches two separately written recomputations on {equal} of {identities} identities, and every other difference has a known cause.
explained.tdh.check.verdict.knownCauseDe: The Rust core and the Python reference agree with each other. Where 6529.io differs, each record is a known difference of class A or B.
explained.tdh.check.verdict.liveDiffers: 6529.io differs from both recomputations on {differ} of {identities} identities.
explained.tdh.check.verdict.liveDiffersD: The Rust core and the Python reference agree with each other. The difference from 6529.io has no known cause, so an alarm is raised.
explained.tdh.check.verdict.programsDiff: The two recomputations differ from each other on {differ} of {identities} identities.
A difference between the Rust core and the Python reference is a defect in one of them, class C, so an alarm is raised.
explained.tdh.check.verdict.notCompared: The two recomputations were not compared with 6529.io on this day.
explained.tdh.check.verdict.notComparedD: 6529.io's signed upload for this day could not be read, so the day says nothing about 6529.io's TDH. The receipt has what the two programs computed.
explained.tdh.check.verdict.unknown: This day's file reports a verdict this page does not know: {verdict}.
explained.tdh.check.verdict.unknownDetai: Its receipt shows every count and hash the file holds.
explained.tdh.check.limit.title: Not guaranteed: that the logs are Ethereum's.
explained.tdh.check.limit.body: All three read Ethereum's logs as public log servers report them; nothing checks those logs against Ethereum's block headers yet.
explained.tdh.check.eq.label: Total TDH, cycle {cycle}
explained.tdh.check.sim.headline: 6529.io differs from both recomputations on {differ} of {identities} identities.
explained.tdh.check.sim.detail: The Rust core and the Python reference agree with each other. 6529.io's records for {differ} identities are {lower} TDH lower: class {class}, no known cause, so an alarm is raised.
explained.tdh.check.ribbon.caption: Each tile is one result: the day held, closed by the {midnight} snapshot on its right edge.
explained.tdh.check.ribbon.rewritten: ↻ marks a file rewritten after its run: {groups}.
explained.tdh.check.ribbon.window: The newest {shown} of {total} days are drawn.
explained.tdh.check.ribbon.all: All {count} days, each with its receipt
explained.tdh.check.ribbon.allLabel: Every day since the first result
explained.tdh.check.ribbon.missing: ◌ marks a day with no published result, so it has no receipt.
explained.tdh.check.runs.label: How the check runs
explained.tdh.check.runs.title: One input, two programs, one comparison.
explained.tdh.check.runs.body: Why two programs? A mistake in one is unlikely to be repeated the same way by a program written separately, so a mistake shows up as a disagreement. 6529.io is then compared with both.
explained.tdh.check.lanes.label: The day's pipeline
explained.tdh.check.lanes.liveCap: its Arweave upload, signed by its key · {hash}
explained.tdh.check.agree.caption: Only the comparisons the run makes are drawn.
explained.tdh.check.agree.rootsSame: The Python reference has no hash tree, so it computes no roots; its records equal the Rust core's byte for byte, which commits it to the same roots.
explained.tdh.check.agree.rootsDiffer: The Python reference has no hash tree, so it computes no roots; on this day its records are not the Rust core's byte for byte.
explained.tdh.check.classes.name: Class {name}
explained.tdh.check.classes.a: A known, deliberate difference between TDH v1.4 and 6529.io's old code.
explained.tdh.check.classes.b: A known bug in 6529.io's old code.
explained.tdh.check.classes.c: The two programs disagree: a defect in one of them. Raises an alarm.
explained.tdh.check.classes.d: 6529.io differs, with no known cause. Raises an alarm.
explained.tdh.check.classes.none: On every day so far there is no difference of any class.
explained.tdh.check.classes.some: On {days} of the {total} days so far some record differs; each day's receipt counts its differences by class.
explained.tdh.check.classes.known: The list of known differences has been empty since transaction netting (D131), so any difference from 6529.io raises an alarm.
explained.tdh.check.read.label: Read it right
explained.tdh.check.read.title: A green day is a strong check, not a proof.
explained.tdh.check.read.body: Here is exactly how far it goes.
explained.tdh.check.read.shows1: 6529.io's TDH for every identity equals two separately written computations, to the unit.
explained.tdh.check.read.shows2: The files compared are the ones the index lists: you can recompute each file's hash.
explained.tdh.check.read.shows3: 6529.io's upload is signed by its Arweave key, so you can check who published it.
explained.tdh.check.read.not1Title: That Ethereum's history was read correctly.
explained.tdh.check.read.not1: All three take the logs as public log servers report them.
explained.tdh.check.read.not2: Its files are hashed, not signed.
explained.tdh.check.read.not4Title: A second reading of the logs.
explained.tdh.check.read.not4: Both programs read one input file, written by the Rust core. Once 6529.io cuts over to the Rust core, planned for about {cutover}, nothing re-reads the logs separately until outside validators run.
explained.tdh.check.read.not4Late: Both programs read one input file, written by the Rust core. The move of 6529.io to the Rust core's result was planned for about {cutover} and, as of {checked}, has not been made. Once it is, nothing re-reads the logs separately until outside validators run.
explained.tdh.check.self.label: Check it yourself
explained.tdh.check.self.title: Who can repeat each step today.
explained.tdh.check.self.body: Three of the seven steps anyone can repeat now, and one more from the specification. Three need source code that is not public yet: the validator code is published when the owner decides (D116), with no date set.
explained.tdh.check.trail.liveSub: signed on Arweave; sum its rows
explained.tdh.check.cmd.label: Check this day's file
explained.tdh.check.build.label: Build your own TDH
explained.tdh.check.build.body: The {specification} restates the rules in full. Match every identity's final TDH and the totals, then compare record by record with 6529.io's signed upload to find any miss. The day's {size}-byte cycle root, {root}, needs encodings that are not public yet (P28, P11). {vectors}.

explained.tdh.check.hwk.feedDiffers: {count} of the files read do not match the index's SHA-256.
explained.tdh.check.hwk.liveBody: The identity file it signs and uploads to Arweave each day; SHA-256 {hash}.
explained.tdh.check.hwk.decisionsBody: D116 (the code's publication), D121 and D132 (the comparison and the cutover), D131 (netting).
